# CYBR LIGHT live demo

The default view is the real current RGB WebGPU path tracer. Use the scene selector for three procedural transport proofs, four native-authored browser studies, the original GEO exports, and the cleared six-module instrument including cached FLIP frames. The model gallery is the 39-model cleared subset; no substitute geometry is used.

The Forest raster link opens the actual procedural stand: original geometry, 1,220,375 original instance placements, cached sun shadows and approximate sky lighting. It is rasterization, not spectral/path-tracing parity. The forest path-traced reference remains available through the original controls and depends on sufficient browser/GPU limits.

All restored runtime assets are byte-checked against the preserved current capture. Large gzip streams are delivered as static parts and concatenated before the original decoder sees them. No mesh, instance, material, fluid frame or shader math is downsampled or rewritten. The live build adds the large-file delivery adapter, filters unavailable scene choices, and includes settings-preserving GPU-session recovery with mobile compilation/timing policy. Original renderer implementation digests are retained separately. See [mobile recovery](MOBILE_GPU_RECOVERY.md) for the tested changes and physical-device limits.

Original forest authoring state and exporter are outside standalone LIGHT. Exact runtime restoration is verified; regeneration from authoring source is a different workflow. Cached FLIP is recorded geometry, not live fluid simulation.

The composite instrument's four files match the cleared public portfolio package exactly. Current MakeHuman/Quaternius mannequin provenance and motion credits are retained under LICENSES. Source/code GPLv2, original native MIT and meshoptimizer MIT notices remain separate.

Not shipped: Observatory interior/full scene and Drowned Geode exports, their gallery derivatives, and the original pile/million-model bakes that depend on those inputs. Their imported-room/scanned-input attribution is unresolved in the inspected records. Large differential/geode authoring caches and old private Git history are not part of this site. Five geode texture conversions have known source names but no verified license/source records here.

Existing moving optical noise, forest lighting/LOD approximation and clearing-camera branch intersection remain. The initial publication used prior matched hardware validation and current CPU asset/source checks. The subsequent mobile recovery update passed a bounded NVIDIA startup/loss/retry check: raw, temporal and final output matched the preserved version after eight identical frames. Physical Adreno execution remains unverified. This was not an FPS benchmark; no universal FPS guarantee is made.

The downloadable source ZIP contains the complete curated native C++/Python, optional CUDA/OptiX and browser renderer source, plus current publication helpers and documentation, without private Git history or large runtime caches. Native offline build/run commands are in its root README; the asset restoration helper retrieves the pinned cleared runtime inputs. The live client modules and delivery adapter are also served directly by this site.

The [full public repository](https://github.com/cybrdelic/cybr-light-public) also retains the exact cleared runtime files and publication helpers. The Site source package restores those files from its pinned public input manifest before deployment.

Large static parts and a small selected set of original gallery near-detail payloads are fetched directly from the immutable public GitHub asset commit; smaller assets are included directly. The selection is recorded in [DELIVERY.json](DELIVERY.json). Original compressed-stream hashes and forest geometry/placement hashes remain unchanged. The external origin is `raw.githubusercontent.com/cybrdelic/cybr-light-public/965ebafa93e96936f870a43db50d721043cd56da/dist/browser/assets/`. Origin failures appear as loader errors. Clone the full repository to serve all parts locally without this external delivery dependency.
